details: Bitcoin's price has fallen below the $60,000 mark, reaching its lowest level in over two years. This downturn is primarily fueled by record outflows from US spot Bitcoin ETFs, which are nearing $5 billion for November, the largest monthly total since their launch. Weakness in technology stocks and expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes are also contributing to the bearish sentiment.
title: Bitcoin Dips Below $60K as ETF Outflows Hit Record Highs

details: The recent $6.3 billion Binance hack underscored the significant power of stablecoin issuers like Tether and Circle. They quickly froze over $1.5 billion in USDT and $1.1 billion in USDC, respectively, to curb the theft. While these actions limited the damage, they also raised concerns about the centralized control over stablecoins and the challenges users face in recovering frozen funds, with reports of Tether charging a 20% reissuance fee.
title: Binance Hack Exposes Stablecoin Issuers' Control Over Funds
